title: Now called Paddock, with Codex sessions beside Claude Code
notes: Claude Sessions is now Paddock, since it is no longer only for Claude: the command is paddock. cc-sessions still works, and your accounts, settings and shortcuts have moved over by themselves.
Codex accounts: ~/.codex and any ~/.codex-* folder can be added as accounts (Settings › Accounts lists them under folders not registered yet), or with: paddock account add NAME --tool codex.
Saved Codex conversations are listed, searched and resumed (codex resume) beside Claude Code's, with Codex's own titles, and counted in Usage by model.

Running Codex sessions show as open, working or waiting. Close stops the turn Codex is working on and closes its window; a turn Codex carries on with after its window was closed is listed too, and can be stopped. On Windows, running Codex sessions are not found yet.
The loop check reads Codex's patches and failing commands too.
Accounts show which tool they are for; a Codex account whose name does not say so carries a small Codex mark.
Fixed: on macOS, a key pressed while Resume or Log in opened a terminal window could make the command run as a different account. The line is now cleared first.

title: What's new, in the page
notes: After an update, a What's new window lists the changes in every version since the one you had, instead of a link to GitHub.
Settings › General › Updates has a What's new button to see them again.

title: Loop check: "no change" is not a complaint
notes: "No change" no longer counts as saying a fix failed: it matched questions like "are there no changes in the repo?". Earlier counts are corrected.

title: Spot sessions going round in circles
notes: Worth a look: sessions that may have gone round in circles, from what the transcripts show: the same error coming back after each fix, edits putting back text taken out earlier, many tokens for little changed, and the person saying it still isn't working.
Only sessions with real work in them are judged (20+ replies, 250K+ tokens without cache reads, 5+ edits to the project), against your own usual; spend alone is never enough.

A Worth a look place in the Finder sidebar, a badge on the session, the reasons in Quick Look and the classic details, Loop score in the Sort menu, and Not a loop, which hides it and raises the bar a little.

title: Tokens per prompt
notes: A Per prompt column in the Finder layout's List view: a session's tokens divided by the prompts typed. Sort by it to bring sessions that used a lot for each thing asked to the top.
Folders show their totals' ratio. Also in the Sort menu and in Quick Look.

title: Auto-update, problem reports, editors and column sorting
notes: Auto-update, on by default: once a day it looks for a new release, checks it against the release's SHA-256 list, swaps it in and restarts. Settings › General › Updates, or cc-sessions update.
Report a problem from Settings, from the Report button on any error, or with cc-sessions report: a GitHub issue filled in with version, system and recent errors, with folders left out.
Open a session's folder in VS Code, Cursor, Zed, Windsurf, Sublime Text or a JetBrains IDE, picked in Settings.
Sort the List view by any column, either way.

title: 3D usage model and fixes
notes: The 3D usage view, rebuilt: Angled, Front, Top, Side and Last 30 days views (keys 1-5), full screen, hover and click a day for its tokens and sessions.
Heat maps in blue, green, amber, purple, teal or the primary colour.
The Settings window and the narrow Finder window scroll again.

title: Finder layout, token usage, Settings and icons
notes: A Finder-style layout of the same sessions: Icons, List and Columns views, Quick Look, a right-click menu and Finder's keys.
Token usage from the transcripts: a calendar heat map, when in the week Claude is used, and totals by account, model and session.
One Settings window for both layouts: layout, Light/Dark, templates, a primary colour, accounts and Disconnect.
